name: Gareth Evans

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am a researcher with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government; we sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. Tell me about a normal shift.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 43 and have spent years on calls and chats at the contact centre. I finished secondary school and do the job about as well as most experienced agents, though the pay here sits low. I use AI every day to sort a long chat history, then check the delivery and payment screens myself.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is waiting at home when you finish?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner Imani works at a repair garage, and we have two children in school and a mortgage. We have less than a month of expenses saved. There are few similar centres close by, so I notice every change in the rota even while I enjoy trying a new tool.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau: Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team the note sorter saves me time, but only when the agent checks the current order. I would show a colleague the address error I caught last week so nobody repeats it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my experienced job to stay in this picture, but the mortgage still takes most of our pay. Imani has steady garage hours for now, yet we have less than a month saved. A tiny AI change does not fix a broken car or a school bill.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would keep taking the order calls and checking the AI notes against the latest screen. I would show the team the bad address draft in our normal huddle and save a small fixed amount after each pay. In the first year we would delay buying a newer car.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about money, not the small tool. I can enjoy a quicker note and still count the mortgage days.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why think about a newer car now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our old car starts slowly, and Imani needs it to reach the garage before my shift. We can wait on a replacement, but I would set aside money for a repair.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What did the address draft get wrong?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: It copied the address from the previous order. The customer had moved, and I found that only because I opened the current delivery page.

say: I would say AI notes help after a **current-order check**.
I would show the team the copied **old address**.
think: I expect my experienced **job** to continue.
Our **mortgage** and thin savings still make a car repair risky this year.
do: Keep checking **AI notes** against current orders.
Show the bad **address draft** in the normal huddle.
Save a little and delay a **newer car**.
S0.quote: I can enjoy a quicker note and still count the mortgage days.
fieldNote: He uses AI **daily** but verifies each delivery page.
The old car is both a **work link** and a risk.
His baseline worry is the **mortgage**, not automation.

steps.text: Keep taking order calls and verify AI notes against current delivery pages
Put a fixed small amount into savings after each pay
Delay replacing the old family car during the first year

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption: Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell colleagues easy chats might move before the company knows what the new jobs are. I would ask management for paid hours and vacancy numbers, then judge the new answer system on real orders.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my own hours could fall when routine orders go to software. I am competent, but I am not the only competent agent here, and few centres are nearby. With less than a month saved, even a short cut would reach our mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I would ask for a paid trial of the new answer system and record wrong delivery dates and repeat calls. I would ask management for the staffing plan, then apply for a posted paid account-checking role if my hours fall and its written wage and hours cover the mortgage. I would keep my current shifts until a real offer is signed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the rota and curious about the tool. Testing it will not pay our bills unless there is a job attached.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell Imani if the trial goes well?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would show her the hours on the rota first. A good trial may make me useful, but it does not promise the centre will keep my seat.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you pay for training now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only for a specific posted job if the employer will not fund it and the cost leaves the mortgage money safe. I would ask for paid study time before agreeing to more than a short course.

say: I would ask for **paid-hour figures** and vacancies.
I would test the new system on **real orders** before relying on its answers.
think: My own **hours** could fall as routine orders move from agents to software.
I have few nearby jobs and thin **savings** to protect our mortgage.
do: Test the new **answer system** on paid time.
Apply after lost hours only to **posted account work** with written mortgage-covering wages and hours; keep my wage until signed offer.
S1.quote: A good trial may make me useful, but it does not promise the centre will keep my seat.
fieldNote: He tests real **delivery errors**, not just speed.
A good trial does not guarantee a **seat**.
He keeps his wage until a **signed mortgage-covering offer**.

steps.text: Test the new answer system on paid time and record repeat calls
Apply to posted jobs with written mortgage-covering pay and hours; keep wage until signed offer

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028: Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say AGI by 2028 can answer and check almost every call we handle. I would ask the centre for notice dates and named paid posts before it changes the queues.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my order and payment work could disappear in 2028, long before hands-on robots arrive around 2031. Our savings would not cover a month of bills, and Imani's garage wage cannot carry the mortgage alone. I know the tools now, but full AGI may do this job better and cheaper.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would get the written notice terms and list actual paid vacancies within reach. I would put any extra pay into savings and take a funded course on paid time only if a named posted role requires it. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2028, if my job ends I would apply for paid accounts work with written wages and hours covering our mortgage; I would not leave before an offer is signed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed by the short runway. I can make a spreadsheet of options, but it does not create a wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell the children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell them we may skip weekend trips if my shifts end. I would not tell them their school plans must change on the strength of a forecast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move to another area?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if a signed offer pays enough after housing and travel, and the children have a workable school journey. Moving four people on a job listing is not a plan.

say: I would seek **written notice** and named paid jobs.
I would say **2028** reaches our calls three years before hands-on robots.
think: My order desk could end in **2028** before I have a new wage.
Imani’s wage and our tiny **reserve** cannot carry the mortgage alone for long.
do: List paid **vacancies** and notice terms now; save extra pay.
Take a funded **required course** for a named posted role only on paid time.
Apply for **paid accounts work** after cuts with written mortgage-covering wages and hours; leave only with a signed offer.
S2.quote: I can make a spreadsheet of options, but it does not create a wage.
fieldNote: He separates full thinking AI from later **robots**.
A course needs **funding** and paid time for a named posted role.
A family move needs an **offer** and workable school journey.

steps.text: Take a funded course on paid time only if a named posted role requires it
Put extra pay into savings while the contact centre still pays him
Apply for paid accounts work after a cut; leave only with signed mortgage-covering wages and hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031: Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell colleagues five years gives time to test the jobs the centre says it will keep. I would ask for posted wages and hours before signing up for any course.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I still think many order calls could go in 2031. Five years lets me learn how to check exceptions on paid time and save more if our budget allows. Robots around 2034 come after the screen change for my work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I would ask for a paid trial checking AI order decisions and study the exceptions the quality team flags. I would set aside a fixed part of any overtime and watch posted account-review vacancies. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2031, if calls end I would apply for a paid review job only if written wages and hours cover our mortgage, keeping my current wage until a signed offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious, but the longer warning helps. I can find out whether review work is real before depending on it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you learn in the trial?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would compare the delivery promise, the account record and the actual parcel scan. If the machine is wrong, I want to know which source it ignored.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you buy a review certificate?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not without a posted paid vacancy that requires it and money left after the mortgage. I would ask the employer to fund the course and paid hours first.

say: I would ask for **posted wages and hours**.
I would test whether review jobs have **real tasks** on customer orders.
think: I think order calls may shrink by **2031** when AGI handles customers.
I can build **exception-checking skill** on paid shifts while still earning.
do: Try paid **AI order checks** this year.
Apply after 2031 only to **posted review work** with written mortgage-covering wages and hours; keep my wage until signed offer.
S3.quote: I can find out whether review work is real before depending on it.
fieldNote: He tests the parcel scan against the **delivery promise**.
He will not buy a speculative **certificate**.
A posted review role needs written **wages and hours**.

steps.text: Learn the quality team AI order checks on paid trial shifts if offered
Save a fixed part of overtime pay toward the mortgage reserve
Apply only to posted reviews with written mortgage-covering pay and hours; keep wage until signed offer

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036: Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the floor a decade gives us time to compare real openings, not just collect course badges. I would ask the centre to show what customer appeal work will be paid.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be 53 in 2036, and the children may be older but the mortgage may still be there. I could be working in customer appeals before then, though full AGI could change that work too. The robots around 2039 are later than the screen change.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would keep the paid call shifts and ask for one paid appeal-review trial each month if the centre offers it. I would save toward a full month of expenses and watch real openings twice a year. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2036, if calls go I would apply for a posted paid appeal job only if written wages and hours cover the mortgage; I would leave only after signing an offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about the distant job change and anxious about this month's bills. A decade before AGI is useful only if our pay keeps coming while I prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you put in an appeal record?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The customer's complaint, the machine decision and the correction, with names removed. I want proof that I solved something, not just that I sat beside a new screen.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Do you expect to stop work at 53?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. I have not planned an age to stop earning, and I do not know our mortgage balance in 2036. I would rather plan around actual vacancies.

say: I would ask the centre for paid **appeal work** before the old calls end.
I would compare **real openings** twice yearly over the decade.
think: I may still owe the **mortgage** at 53.
I cannot assume **appeal work** survives full AGI after 2036.
do: Try monthly paid **appeal reviews** if offered.
Apply after 2036 only to **posted appeals work** with written mortgage-covering wages and hours; keep my wage until signed offer.
S4.quote: A decade before AGI is useful only if our pay keeps coming while I prepare.
fieldNote: He rejects invented **retirement timing** and plans around vacancies instead.
The appeal record shows actual **corrections** with customer names removed.
A new role needs a **signed mortgage-covering offer** with written hours and wages.

steps.text: Keep taking paid calls while the centre still staffs the queue
Learn AI appeal review on paid monthly trial shifts if offered
Save toward one full month of household expenses
Apply only to posted appeals with written mortgage-covering pay and hours; keep wage until signed offer

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. I use AI every day, but our savings are shorter than any serious job search. Written notice, a paid role with wages and hours covering the mortgage, and training on paid time tied to a posted opening would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who checks the delivery promise after the software closes the chat. The parcel still has to reach the right door, and a neat sentence cannot carry it there.

headlineQuote: The parcel still has to reach the right door, and a neat sentence cannot carry it there.
portrait: Gareth is a **43-year-old experienced** contact centre agent with secondary school education and average skill.
He has two school-age children and a mortgage with **Imani**, and earns lower pay for this job.
He uses AI **daily**, but has under one month saved and few nearby centres.
He tests new tools early while requiring **paid trials** and signed mortgage-covering job offers.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could erase his order calls before the household can fund a job search.
whatWouldHelp: **Written notice**, paid vacancy-linked training and a signed role with mortgage-covering wages and hours would help.
